remit: attack crowded ideas; prefer better ownership asymmetry
stance_summary: The packet's easy screens are already owned: receive Canada because CA-US 2Y/5Y/10Y sit at 1y extremes, fade 99th-percentile UST yields with real-money 10Y longs, and receive AONIA because two housing headlines say the RBA is capped. CFTC TFF shows AUD futures open interest at a 1y/3y extreme with leveraged funds still net long AUD, while AONIA open interest is piled in the October contract and almost empty by March 2027. That is better ownership asymmetry than adding to the CORRA receive this seat already holds. Close crowded long CORRA_2027-03 and pay AONIA_2027-03.

trade.structure: Pay ASX 30-day AONIA 2027-03 outright in implied-rate space (AONIA_2027-03). Canonical short duration: profits if the packet implied-rate mark rises.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Pay AONIA_2027-03 (short duration / implied AONIA higher). Alternative rates expressions rejected as crowded or inferior: receive CORRA_2027-03 (CA-US value screen plus this book and other paper seats already own the receive); pay SOFR_2027-03/2027-09 (rate-hawk and trend-follower already pay US; asset-manager 10Y longs are the crowd to fade, not join by receiving UST).
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDCAD, the 1y/5y extreme cross that embeds the same crowded AUD-long versus CAD-short ownership.
expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing is an RBA path that housing-consensus receivers have capped near two hikes, not an FX cross that also mixes CAD-specific cheapness and covering CAD shorts. AONIA_2027-03 has a live policy path, a packet mid, and near-empty open interest versus the October battleground. Rates and spot are comparably directional on AUD, so the rates-first rule selects AONIA.

context_build.causal_mechanism: A globally tighter policy impulse (Fed hike delivered, BoJ to 1.25%, energy shock still constraining easing) can keep RBA inflation pressure high even while housing is the advertised transmission channel. Crowded AUD-long and AONIA-receive ownership then has to buy a higher AONIA path if the housing cap fails. Paying the empty 2027-03 contract owns that squeeze without sitting in the October open-interest pile or in the CA-US receive screen.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Verified: AONIA overnight 4.35 as of 17-Sep-2026; Oct-26 implied 4.565 (+21.5bp, open interest 21752, volume 4450); Nov-26 4.685 (+33.5bp); Mar-27 4.86 (+51.0bp, open interest 201, volume 1); Jun-27 4.94 (+59.0bp). AU 2Y 4.999 and 10Y 5.348 as of 2026-09-16, both ~99th percentile 1y and 5y, with 2Y +39.1bp over 1m then a 1d dip. AUDUSD 0.7120, 76th percentile 1y; AUDCAD 0.9976, ~99.8th/99.96th percentile 1y/5y. CFTC AUD futures OI 493141 as of 2026-09-15, 99th percentile 1y/3y, +37673 on the week; leveraged funds net long AUD. Inference: bonds have already paid a hawkish Australia while STIR open interest and news flow still fight the front hike and cap the back.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: Australian housing downturn under higher rates (two retained headlines), AU inflation gauge 82, AU yields already at 1y/5y extremes, AONIA path upward-sloping. Known: Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% was heavily pre-priced then delivered; SOFR fixing 3.85 on 2026-09-17. New enough to change ownership risk now: BoJ 25bp to 1.25% (31-year high), desk thesis that energy/global tightening is constraining the easing impulse, BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through (squeeze risk for the Canada-receive crowd), and CFTC showing AUD OI at a multi-year extreme with CAD leveraged-fund shorts already covering toward a 1y net extreme. The housing story is not new information; it is the consensus that still owns the AONIA receive.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: AONIA prices about one hike by October and about two hikes by March 2027, then almost no additional tightening into mid-2027 (Mar-27 +51bp, Jun-27 +59bp versus overnight). That path assumes housing and activity cap the RBA after roughly two 25bp moves despite an 82 inflation gauge.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that the housing-downturn narrative, already in the tape and in AONIA open interest, is a reason to receive Australian STIRs or to treat ~60bp of terminal tightening as a ceiling. The crowded assumption is that RBA cannot follow the global tightening impulse. Also disagree that CA-US yield extremes are a reason to keep receiving CORRA_2027-03: that is the value/dove/carry ownership this seat should not add to.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: AONIA cash 4.35 versus Mar-27 4.86 is a policy-path premium, not a term-premium 10Y story. Change: AU 2Y/5Y/10Y all sold off ~26-39bp over 1m then eased a few bp on 2026-09-16, while the AONIA strip still concentrates liquidity in October. Cross-market: CA-US 2Y -140bp (3.8th percentile 1y) and CA-US 5Y/10Y at ~0.2nd percentile 1y show Canada already priced as the dove; AUDCAD at a 5y extreme shows AUD already owned versus CAD. Marginal driver for AONIA_2027-03 is whether a third hike/higher terminal is allowed, not whether October prints 21.5bp versus 25bp.

historical_reference.distribution: Verified packet distributions: AU 2Y/5Y/10Y all ~99th percentile 1y and 5y; AU 2s10s 34.9bp, 24th percentile 1y. AUDCAD ~99.8th/99.96th percentile 1y/5y. CFTC AUD OI 99th percentile 1y and 3y (z 3.61/5.42). CAD leveraged-fund net still short but 99th percentile 1y of that net (covering). analogs: Qualitative analog only: RBA 2022-23 continued hiking after housing turnover had already slowed, because inflation persistence dominated the housing-cap narrative. Packet does not reconstruct that episode's AONIA path, so it is a mechanism analog rather than a quantified forward-outcome table.
No fully measured comparable episode with matched AONIA open-interest and CFTC AUD extremes is in this frozen packet; do not treat the 99th-percentile yield or OI prints as a mean-reversion clock.
historical_reference.regime_differences: AONIA overnight is already 4.35, not a near-zero start. Inflation gauge 82 coexists with an ongoing housing downturn, so both sides of the 2022 analog are live at once. CFTC is futures-only TFF, five days old, and MX CORRA / CME SR3 positioning is unavailable. NZ policy path and NZ sovereigns are missing, so this is not an AU-NZ rates RV.

policy_path_check.pricing_summary: AU: AONIA 4.35; Oct-26 4.565 (+21.5bp); Mar-27 4.86 (+51bp); Jun-27 4.94 (+59bp). US: SOFR 3.85 after the 3.75-4.00% funds range; SR3 Mar-27 4.58 (+73bp); SR3 Sep-27 4.755 (+90.5bp, local peak). CA: CORRA 2.29; CRAH27 / CORRA_2027-03 3.13 (+84bp); mid-2028 ~3.65 (+136bp). NZ path unavailable.
policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end AU trade must start from the AONIA strip, not from AU 2Y percentiles. The strip is live and shows the housing-cap priced as a two-hike ceiling. US and CA paths are context for why global tightening can leak into RBA odds and why the existing CORRA receive is the crowded Canada-dove expression being closed, not the debate trade.

trade.thesis: FACT: AONIA prices ~51bp of tightening by Mar-27 and ~59bp by Jun-27 against overnight 4.35, with open interest 21752 in Oct-26 versus 201 in Mar-27; AU inflation gauge 82; housing-downturn headlines are already in the packet; CFTC AUD futures OI is a 1y/3y extreme with leveraged funds still net long AUD; paper books already receive AONIA and CORRA. INFERENCE: the tradeable discrepancy is not 'Australia is hawkish' as a fresh macro call — bonds already show that — it is that housing-consensus receivers and crowded AUD longs own the fade of further RBA tightening, leaving Mar-27 AONIA as the cleaner squeeze if global tightening (Fed delivered, BoJ 1.25%, energy still a constraint) forces a higher Australian terminal. UNKNOWN: side of AONIA October open interest, MX CORRA specs, CME SR3 specs, and any post-2026-09-15 CFTC change. This seat therefore pays AONIA_2027-03 and closes the crowded CORRA receive rather than adding to CA-US value.
trade.mispricing: FACT: Mar-27 AONIA implied 4.86 versus cash 4.35 (+51bp) and versus AU 2Y 4.999. INFERENCE: the back of the AONIA curve still treats housing as a hard cap after two hikes, while inflation, global policy, and AUD ownership argue that cap is the consensus, not an edge. The October contract is the wrong place to pay (21.5bp of a 25bp hike already in, and that is where OI lives). UNKNOWN: whether RBA's next meeting calendar maps a full 25bp into the March window versus a later contract; packet gives implied rates not a meeting-probability model.
why_now: Housing-stops-RBA is dual-headline consensus, not a new shock, while AU inflation remains the hottest four-country gauge.
CFTC AUD open interest is at a 1y/3y extreme with leveraged funds still net long; AUDCAD is at a 5y extreme — the long-AUD complex is owned.
AONIA open interest is concentrated in October; Mar-27 is an ownership vacuum with a live implied-rate mark.
Desk thesis plus BoJ 1.25% and a delivered Fed hike tighten the global easing constraint now, which is when housing receivers get run if they are wrong.
This book already owns long CORRA_2027-03, which sits inside the CA-US extreme-value crowd after BoC energy-pass-through minutes; adding another receive would be duplicate crowded ownership.
